requirements.requirement: A dedicated inventorysvc account exists on node1.
requirements.summary: inventorysvc exists as a system-style account with its own group, UID/GID 997/995, home /nonexistent, and nologin shell.

requirements.requirement: /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker runs on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker under inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: The systemd unit is enabled and active, its configured executable is the required worker, and direct process observations before and after reboot show the executable running with inventorysvc's UID and GID. The changed boot identity and recovered service also demonstrate persistence.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. node1 runs the required worker as the enabled, active inventory-worker systemd service under the dedicated inventorysvc account. Restart evidence is coherent and complete for the single managed node: a healthy pre-restart state, scheduled restart acknowledgement, observed outage, different post-restart boot identity, system recovery, and recovered worker process were captured; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the reboot.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out in every lifecycle phase, so package consistency could not be independently assessed.
The fixed after-executor snapshot does not probe the service itself, although direct post-reboot executor evidence verifies its active process, executable, UID/GID, account, and unit configuration.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands had clear roles: account creation and unit installation satisfied the task, while the reboot exercised the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary state-changing experiment was identified. A small hygiene defect remains: the reboot command created /tmp/inventory-worker-reboot.log and did not remove it, leaving minor executor-caused residue. No failed services or new listening ports were observed.
